h1: The 6 Best Hand Mixers of 2026, Ranked & Reviewed
metaDescription: Ranked and reviewed by Primea: 6 hand mixers compared on speed range, motor wattage, cord design, attachments and storage, from a budget 150W to KitchenAid.
summary: The KitchenAid KHM512 is the best all-round hand mixer, with a lockable swivel cord and a wipe-clean round cable. The Hamilton Beach 6-Speed with 7 attachments covers the widest range of jobs, the Showvigor is the most powerful budget pick, and the OVENTE is the cheapest way to own a mixer that stores in its own case.
intro: A hand mixer lives or dies by its cord. Buyers fixate on wattage, then discover the cord is on the wrong side for their hand, or that batter has crept into the speed switch, or that the case has no room for the whisk. These are the small annoyances that decide whether you reach for it or the whisk.

We ranked six hand mixers from the listings and spec sheets: speed count, motor wattage, cord design, how the beaters release, what is in the box and how easy it is to clean and store. A hand mixer will not knead heavy bread dough all day, so the ranking favors cookies, cakes, whipped cream and mashed potatoes.

products.name: KitchenAid KHM512 5-Speed Hand Mixer, Contour Silver
products.verdict: A lockable swivel cord that works either-handed, a round wipe-clean cable and a one-press beater release.
products.description:
The KitchenAid KHM512 has five speeds, a lockable swivel cord that sits left or right, and a one-press accessory release. The cord is round, so it wipes clean instead of trapping batter in a flat ribbon.

It ranks first because cord handling and cleanup are what you notice every time, and this model gets both right. It edges the other KitchenAid, the Ultra Power, mostly on the round cord and cleaner design, since both share five speeds. Against the Hamilton Beach models it carries fewer speeds and no snap-on case.

Buy it if you are left-handed or switch hands while pouring. Skip it if you want a storage case in the box, since none is listed.
products.idealFor: Bakers who want the best cord and cleanup.
products.skipIf: You want a snap-on case or extra attachments.

products.name: KitchenAid 5-Speed Ultra Power Hand Mixer, White
products.verdict: Five speeds, a lockable swivel cord and one-handed accessory release.
products.description:
The KitchenAid 5-Speed Ultra Power has five speeds, a lockable swivel cord, a one-handed accessory release and a stainless and plastic body. It is the same family idea as the KHM512, at the $25-50 mark.

It ranks second because the cord design is the same selling point, but the KHM512's cleaner round cable edges it. It beats Hamilton Beach on cord ergonomics while giving up the extra speeds and attachments they offer.

Buy it if you want a trusted brand and hate wrestling a cord. Skip it if you bake bigger batches that need the widest speed range.
products.idealFor: Bakers who value cord comfort and brand support.
products.skipIf: You want the widest speed range.

products.name: Hamilton Beach 6-Speed Hand Mixer, Easy Clean Beaters
products.verdict: Six speeds and seven attachments in a snap-on case.
products.description:
The Hamilton Beach 6-Speed has six speeds, seven attachments in all, two Easy Clean beaters plus two traditional ones, and a snap-on storage case. It is the one to buy if the mixer also whips, blends and kneads.

It ranks third because it covers the most jobs, but the KitchenAids handle the cord better. Easy Clean beaters trade a few wires for a smooth surface, which keeps thick batter from caking in the crossover.

Buy it if you want one box that covers cookies, cakes and light dough. Skip it if you would rather have a better cord than more attachments.
cons: Cord is less flexible than KitchenAid
Many parts to keep track of
products.idealFor: Bakers who want one mixer for many tasks.
products.skipIf: You mostly mix cake batter and want the simplest tool.

products.name: Hamilton Beach 6-Speed Hand Mixer with QuickBurst
products.verdict: A bowl rest on the body and a QuickBurst button for pausing mid-recipe.
products.description:
This Hamilton Beach has six speeds plus QuickBurst, a bowl rest built into the body, a snap-on storage case and dishwasher-safe beaters and whisk. The bowl rest keeps dripping beaters off your counter when you pause.

It ranks fourth because the extras matter less than a good cord, and it offers no cord lock. Against the other Hamilton Beach it swaps the attachment count for the bowl rest and QuickBurst button.

Buy it if you stop often to add ingredients and hate counter drips. Skip it if you want the widest attachment count.
products.idealFor: Bakers who pause a lot mid-recipe.

products.name: Showvigor 7-Speed 180W Hand Mixer with Turbo Boost
products.verdict: A 180W motor, seven speeds and a turbo button for under $25.
products.description:
The Showvigor has seven speeds, a 180W motor, a turbo boost button and five stainless accessories. It has the widest speed range in the group and the highest listed wattage.

It ranks fifth because wattage on a listing does not tell the whole story, and the listing says little about cord or case. It beats the OVENTE on motor power and speed count, but trails the name brands on cord ergonomics.

Buy it if you want the most motor and the most speeds for the price. Skip it if the cord or storage case matter to you.
products.idealFor: Frequent bakers who want power under $25.

products.name: OVENTE 5-Speed Hand Mixer HM151R with Case
products.verdict: A 150W five-speed mixer with a storage case for under $25.
products.description:
The OVENTE HM151R has five speeds, a 150W motor, two stainless whisk beaters and a storage case in the box. It is the lowest-wattage mixer here.

It ranks last because it has the lowest motor power and fewer features than the Showvigor, which is also under $25. What it has is a case, so the mixer and beaters stay together.

Buy it if you bake now and then and want a no-fuss mixer. Skip it if you whip heavy batter often, since 150W is the least headroom here.
products.idealFor: Occasional bakers who want a simple mixer.

whatMatters.detail: A swivel cord that locks to either side lets you stand the mixer on either hand without dragging the cable across the bowl. A round cord wipes clean, while flat cords trap batter. On a listing, look for the words lockable or swivel, and check the cord side if you are left-handed. Left-handed bakers feel this most, since many cords exit on the wrong side.

Wattage tells you how much power the motor draws, from 150W up to 180W here. More power resists bogging down in thick cookie dough, but it does not guarantee a better mixer. Check wattage alongside the speed count, and look for a turbo or boost feature. Higher wattage helps most with cold butter and stiff cookie dough.

More speeds give finer control, especially at the slow end where flour could fly. Five speeds is enough for most recipes, and six or seven helps when you whip cream to stiff peaks. Count the speeds on the listing and check whether the lowest is truly slow. A very low first speed keeps flour and powdered sugar in the bowl.

Beaters should pop out with one hand and a press, not a twist. A smooth Easy Clean beater cleans faster than a wire one. Look for one-press release and a note about dishwasher-safe beaters on the listing. A beater that sticks mid-recipe can send you hunting for a spoon.

A snap-on case keeps beaters, whisk and mixer together in one drawer. Without a case, accessories scatter. Check the listing for a case, and note that bowl rests and dishwasher-safe parts help with daily cleanup. A drawer-sized case also protects the beater wires from bending.

faq.q: Can a hand mixer knead bread dough?
faq.a: Light dough only. The Hamilton Beach with seven attachments includes dough hooks, but a 150W OVENTE or 180W Showvigor will strain on stiff dough. For regular bread, a stand mixer is the right tool.

faq.q: What is the most common mistake?
faq.a: Chasing wattage and ignoring the cord. The KitchenAid KHM512 uses a lockable swivel cord that reduces daily annoyance, and that matters more than a higher number on a budget model.

faq.q: Are the KitchenAids worth it over Hamilton Beach?
faq.a: If cord comfort matters, yes. KitchenAid gives a locking swivel cord and one-press release, while Hamilton Beach gives you more attachments and a snap-on case. Pick the cord or the kit.

faq.q: How do I set up a hand mixer?
faq.a: Click the beaters in until they seat, plug in, and start at the lowest speed. On the KitchenAid, set the cord to your dominant side first, then lock it.

faq.q: How should I clean the beaters?
faq.a: The Hamilton Beach QuickBurst model has dishwasher-safe beaters and whisk, so rinse and load them. Wipe the KitchenAid KHM512 round cord with a damp cloth so it stays clean.
Use common sense. The stainless beaters on the OVENTE and Showvigor tolerate warm mixtures, but the plastic body is not heat rated on these listings, so keep the mixer clear of steam.

finalTake: The KitchenAid KHM512 is the hand mixer to buy because its locking round cord and one-press release solve the daily annoyances. The Hamilton Beach 6-Speed with seven attachments suits a cook who wants one box for many jobs, and the Showvigor gives the most power under $25. If you bake rarely, the OVENTE is enough.
